item.title: CENTCOM chief visits USS Abraham Lincoln amid morale concerns
item.description: Meanwhile, Israel is being condemned by Lebanese leaders for strikes in the south that killed at least 11 people, including children.

item.title: Doctor recommends kids get eye exams early to detect vision problems as school years begin
item.description: August marks Children's Eye Health and Safety Month, putting the spotlight on protecting children's vision and eye health. Pediatric ophthalmologists remind parents to check their kids' eyes as they head back to the classroom. CBS News' Michael George reports.

item.title: Indiana storms linked to 7 deaths as floods trigger rescues and evacuations
item.description: Nearly 130,000 utility customers statewide remained without power as of Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Some states crack down on misleading home listings, spruced up with AI
item.description: More home listings are using AI to add furniture, repaint walls, spruce up landscaping and even add windows. But when does virtual staging cross the line into deception or even fraud? CBS News' Evyn Moon explores.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lala brings drenching rain, wind across the Hawaiian Islands
item.description: As a hurricane, Lala skirted past Hawaii's Big Island, where it brought heavy rain and the possibility of life-threatening flooding and mudslides.

item.title: Jared Kushner met with Hamas leaders in Egypt to discuss Gaza peace deal
item.description: Jared Kushner, who is President Trump's son-in-law, is set to meet next with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who rejected the latest peace proposal last week.

item.title: Tommy John, MLB All-Star pitcher who had a surgery named after him, dies at 83
item.description: One of Tommy John's biggest legacies to MLB was his comeback elbow reconstruction surgery that now bears his name.

item.description: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear said he hasn't heard back from Sen. Mitch McConnell following formal requests for an update on his health last month amid a weekslong hospitalization.

item.title: Beshear says U.S. needs to "fix the darn government," including abolishing Electoral College
item.description: Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear, who is the chairman of the Democratic Governors Association, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that the American people think the "government is broken," the U.S. needs to "fix the darn government," including with the election of president and vice president.

item.title: Bacon says Congress "should have oversight" amid concerns about USS Lincoln
item.description: GOP Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska said Congress should conduct oversight following concerns about conditions aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, which is being replaced after a nearly nine-month deployment.

item.title: CBS News political panel on trends being seen so far in midterm elections
item.description: Wall Street Journal reporter Sabrina Rodriguez, NOTUS reporter Paul Kane, The Atlantic staff writer Toluse Olorunnipa and Anthony Salvanto, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys joined "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" to discuss socialism and the Democratic Party, as well as other trends being seen so far in the midterm elections.

item.title: Democratic socialist candidate Chris Rabb says U.S. "is not a purely capitalistic society"
item.description: Pennsylvania state Rep. Chris Rabb, who is a democratic socialist and running for Congress in Pennsylvania's heavily Democratic 3rd District, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that the U.S. "is not a purely capitalistic society," pointing to social programs such as Social Security, public education and more.

item.title: CBS News poll looks at whether Democrats are split over socialism
item.description: As Democrats debate the future of the party amid primaries this summer, CBS News executive director of elections and surveys Anthony Salvanto joins "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" to discuss whether Democrats are split on socialism -- and how Americans see political parties in today's economy.

item.title: Rep. Don Bacon says Trump was "setting maybe false expectations" in initial days of Iran war
item.description: Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska, who is not running for reelection, told "Face the Nation with Margaret Brennan" that President Trump's comments about gas prices amid the Iran war are "honest," and that the president was "setting maybe false expectations in the previous months, during the initial parts of this campaign with Iran."

item.title: Short pants: The long and the short of it
item.description: The summer of 1936 saw a heat wave so dangerous at least five thousand people died. It also saw the popularization of a cooler fashion alternative – shorts – which, in some jurisdictions, were illegal.

item.title: South Carolina to hold first 2028 Democratic presidential primary
item.description: South Carolina's Democratic presidential primary will take place on Jan. 22, 2028. Nevada, New Hampshire, New Mexico, Michigan and Virginia will also hold early Democratic nominating contests.

item.description: This 23-year-old who grew up in a conservative Amish community and had never used a cell phone or computer is today an unlikely social media influencer, sharing stories and recipes of the Amish with her six million online followers.
